title: Venezuela Frees Political Prisoners — and People Want Elections Next
summary:
Imagine being put in prison for disagreeing with your country's leader. In Venezuela, that has happened to many people — they are called "political prisoners."

On Saturday morning, Venezuelan authorities released a group of them. Human rights groups say it was a "significant number" from several detention centres. One man freed was Wilder Vasquez, who got a five-year sentence in 2018 over claims he was plotting to kill former President Nicolás Maduro. Another was Miguel Castillo Cedeño, held since June 2019. A third, Frank Cabañas, had been in prison for nine years.

Why now? Days earlier, Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodríguez met U.S. President Donald Trump at the UN General Assembly in New York. Trump captured Maduro earlier this year. Releasing prisoners and holding free elections were two promises Rodríguez's government made to the U.S.

Her government had already freed hundreds of prisoners as part of a reconciliation effort. But in April, she said the program was "coming to an end." Rights group Foro Penal says it stopped with less than half of Venezuela's political prisoners released.

Venezuela's government hasn't said whether Saturday's releases came from the Trump meeting. It denies that dissidents are jailed at all, and calls the releases a gesture of goodwill. Opposition groups say that's not enough — they want elections, and soon.
why_it_matters: Being able to disagree with your leaders without being locked up is one of the basic things a fair country promises, so what happens in Venezuela shows how important that promise is.

questions.question: What does the story mean by 'political prisoners'?
options: People who are put in prison for disagreeing with their country's leader
People who steal money from banks
People who refuse to pay taxes
People who travel without a passport
questions.correct_answer: People who are put in prison for disagreeing with their country's leader

questions.question: What happened in Venezuela on Saturday morning?
options: The country closed its borders
Authorities released a group of political prisoners
A new president was elected
All the prisoners escaped
questions.correct_answer: Authorities released a group of political prisoners

questions.question: Wilder Vasquez got a five-year sentence in 2018 over what claim?
options: That he sold food without a licence
That he stole a car
That he tried to leave the country
That he was plotting to kill former President Nicolás Maduro
questions.correct_answer: That he was plotting to kill former President Nicolás Maduro

questions.question: Where did interim President Delcy Rodríguez meet U.S. President Donald Trump?
options: At the UN General Assembly in New York
At the White House in Washington
In Caracas
In Miami
questions.correct_answer: At the UN General Assembly in New York

questions.question: What does the rights group Foro Penal say?
options: No one was ever released
The releases stopped with less than half of Venezuela's political prisoners freed
The prisoners refused to leave
Every political prisoner has been freed
questions.correct_answer: The releases stopped with less than half of Venezuela's political prisoners freed

questions.question: What do opposition groups say they want next?
options: A longer school year
A new currency
More prisons
Elections, and soon

background_read: Venezuela (a country in South America) was led by Nicolás Maduro for more than a decade; after a 2024 election that many countries said was not fair, he lost the support of the United States and was captured this year.
The United Nations (a group where almost all countries meet to talk about world problems) holds a big meeting in New York every year called the General Assembly, where leaders give speeches.
Foro Penal is a Venezuelan human rights group (a team that watches how people are treated) that keeps count of political prisoners and pushes governments to free them.
Article_Structure: WHO: Freed prisoners including Wilder Vasquez, Miguel Castillo Cedeño and Frank Cabañas; interim President Delcy Rodríguez; U.S. President Donald Trump; and the rights group Foro Penal.
WHAT: Venezuela released a 'significant number' of political prisoners on Saturday morning, days after Rodríguez met Trump at the UN General Assembly in New York.
WHERE: Venezuela, with releases from several detention centres, after a meeting between the two leaders at the UN General Assembly in New York.
WHY: Releasing prisoners and holding free elections were promises Rodríguez's government made to the U.S., but opposition groups say the releases are not enough and want elections soon.

perspectives.description: It calls the releases a gesture of goodwill, denies that dissidents are jailed at all, and has not said whether the releases came from the meeting with Trump.
They say freeing some prisoners is not enough — they want free elections, and soon.
Foro Penal keeps count and says the release program was said to be 'coming to an end' in April and stopped with less than half of Venezuela's political prisoners freed.
